title: Sport science teacher
description: Company Description High school is an educational institution dedicated to providing inclusive, quality secondary education to learners from diverse backgrounds. The school focuses on strong academic foundations, personal development, and preparation for higher education and future careers. It promotes a supportive environment where students can grow intellectually, socially, and physically. Educators are encouraged to use modern teaching methods, collaborate with colleagues, and participate in school-wide initiatives. The school values professionalism, continuous learning, and positive engagement with students and families. Role Description The Sport Science Teacher is responsible for delivering engaging, curriculum-aligned lessons that integrate concepts from sport science, physics, and mathematics. This full-time, on-site role in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia includes planning and preparing lessons, assessing student progress, and providing constructive feedback to support learning. The teacher will design practical activities, demonstrations, and assessments that promote physical literacy, scientific understanding of movement, and healthy lifestyle choices. Daily responsibilities include maintaining a safe learning environment, recording grades, communicating with parents and guardians when needed, and collaborating with colleagues on cross-curricular projects. The role also involves participating in staff meetings, professional development, and school events related to sports and academic enrichment. Qualifications Strong background in Science Education, with the ability to teach Sport Science in a high school setting. Subject knowledge in Physics and Mathematics to integrate scientific and quantitative concepts into sport-related lessons. Qualified Teacher status or equivalent teaching certification, with experience teaching at the secondary level. Proficiency in Lesson Planning, including designing engaging, inclusive, and assessment-driven lessons. Excellent classroom management, communication, and interpersonal skills to support a diverse student body. Ability to create safe and inclusive practical learning environments, particularly in sports and physical activities. Bachelor’s degree or higher in Sport Science, Physical Education, Science Education, or a closely related field. Experience or interest in coaching school sports teams or leading extracurricular physical activities is an advantage. Commitment to continuous professional development and collaboration with colleagues and school leadership.MSC sprt sciene

title: Cabin Engineer - Ethiopia Recruitment Event
description: Special Note – Ethiopia Recruitment Event This vacancy is linked to Air Arabia’s upcoming invitation-only Engineering Recruitment Event in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Candidates should apply to this vacancy only if they are available to attend the recruitment event in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia mid November 2026, subject to being shortlisted and invited by Air Arabia. Full event details, including venue, date, timing and interview schedule, will be shared only with shortlisted candidates prior to the event. If you are interested in similar Air Arabia opportunities but are not available to attend the Ethiopia event, please apply separately to the relevant non-event vacancy on the Air Arabia careers site. Job Purpose Carries out and supervises Cabin Appearance Base-level maintenance tasks on Air Arabia and Third-party aircraft within the corresponding License Category, ensuring the required work is performed, certified and recorded accurately and timely in accordance with Air Arabia and regulatory requirements. Key Result Responsibilities Operational Excellence Constantly verifies and ensures compatibility and readiness of cabin appearance components as per approved standards and quantity to be used as and when needed. Reviews assigned task cards with the Workshop Supervisor to gain full understanding of the work, priorities, documentation requirements and cautions, prior to starting work. Prepares and performs scheduled cabin appearance maintenance according to assigned task cards, ensuring feasibility and cost effectiveness; ensures that the required documentation, parts, tools and GSE are obtained and used per issued instructions (wherever applicable). Carries out component (cabin appearance) test and inspection tasks to the standard necessary to fully identify and record any defects or damage in accordance with approved maintenance procedures. Performs defect rectification in accordance with Aircraft Approved Data and instructions provided by the Engineering Department. Signs of maintenance tasks performed or supervised within the scope of own authorization, verifying that the task card and associated documents have been completed to the required standard following completion of all maintenance. Manages communications with other Engineers and Technicians related to the assigned tasks, ensuring proper coordination, continuity and handover of work Safety Manages the safety of assigned maintenance tasks, ensuring all published mandatory precautions are taken prior to commencing work and during task execution. Take positive steps to protect self and other people in the area of maintenance activity from any possible injury, including the use of proper GSE and protective equipment. Manages human factors aspects of maintenance, ensuring that the continuity of critical maintenance tasks is protected, by avoidance of task interruption and the proper use of handover procedures. Reputation And Teamwork Internal Customer Service: provides positive support to other operational teams in ABY, provides proactive and helpful professional advice, suggestions and solutions. Leadership: provides sound supervision and guidance to Technicians assigned to support their own tasks. Ensure they are adequately briefed to perform the non-certifying maintenance tasks. Representing Air Arabia: presents a positive and competent image of technical professionalism to ABY Flight Crews, other companies’ personnel and ABY customers. Cost Awareness Maintains positive awareness to the cost of aircraft maintenance including use of time and materials. Minimizes unnecessary waste of consumable material and part repair cost by avoiding unnecessary damage and repeat work during maintenance. Working Relationships/Communication. People Management Provides direction, coaching and guidance to team members for their career and professional development. Creates a conducive working environment to build and sustain a performance driven, engaged, and committed team. Ensures people management responsibilities are handled effectively in line with company procedures. Qualifications (Academic, Training, Languages) Holds / has held a valid EASA/GCAA/CAA/ICAO Maintenance Engineer’s licence is an advantage. Ability to use a computer (Microsoft Office). Ability to obtain Driver’s License in work location. Ability to read, write, speak and understand English to a very good standard for technical communications. Work Experience Extensive working experience in similar role in a workshop. With at least 2 years’ experience qualified maintenance technician on the Airbus A320/A321 family of aircraft or at least 4 years’ experience in a Base Maintenance or Workshop Maintenance environment.

title: Director, International & Public Affairs, African Union, Addis Ababa Ethiopia
organization: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
description: Job Description The Director, African Union Office, serves as the Church's senior representative to the African Union and leads the Church's diplomatic and public affairs presence in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The director develops enduring relationships with African Union institutions, member-state missions, diplomatic representatives, nongovernmental organizations, faith-based organizations, and trusted partners. The role ensures accurate representation of Church positions, coordinates appropriate engagement by Church leaders and affiliated humanitarian entities, and provides on-the-ground leadership, continuity, institutional memory, and operational oversight for the office. Responsibilities Develop and execute an approved engagement plan for the African Union, diplomatic missions, relevant multilateral bodies, nongovernmental organizations, and faith-based partners. Represent the Church professionally in authorized diplomatic, public affairs, interfaith, humanitarian, and civil-society settings. Build sustained, trust-based relationships and maintain accurate stakeholder maps, engagement histories, priorities, and follow-up records. Coordinate with Church headquarters with providing timely political, social, humanitarian, religious-freedom, and reputational context relevant to African Union engagement to Africa Area leadership. Prepare briefing materials, official correspondence, meeting strategies, visit programs, reports, and recommendations for Church leaders and headquarters teams. Coordinate with Area leadership of all Africa-based Area presidencies, headquarters departments, diplomatic offices, and affiliated humanitarian entities to ensure unity, clarity, and appropriate approvals. Lead office operations, personnel, budgets, security, protocols, records, facilities, vendors, and compliance with applicable Church policies and local requirements. Plan and support visits, consultations, events, and delegations involving senior Church leaders and external dignitaries. Monitor commitments, emerging issues, and partnership opportunities; elevate risks and sensitive matters promptly through established channels. Manage employees and mixed-workforce resources and, in partnership with Human Resources, make recommendations regarding hiring, performance, advancement, and changes in status. Required QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in international relations, diplomacy, public policy, law, political science, public affairs, African studies, development, or a related field, or equivalent education and experience. Ten or more years of progressively responsible experience in diplomacy, multilateral affairs, government relations, international public affairs, humanitarian engagement, or a related field. Demonstrated experience working with senior government, diplomatic, multilateral, faith, or civil-society leaders in Africa. Strong understanding of African Union institutions, diplomatic protocol, regional dynamics, stakeholder engagement, and international development or humanitarian issues. Exceptional judgment, discretion, cultural intelligence, relationship management, writing, briefing, negotiation, and public representation skills. Proven ability to operate independently in a complex international environment while remaining closely aligned with authorized direction. Experience managing an office, staff, budgets, security considerations, visits, events, and sensitive records. Fluency in English and ability to work effectively across linguistic and cultural settings. Sound knowledge of Church doctrine, organization, policy, and humanitarian and public affairs objectives. Ability and legal eligibility to reside and work in Addis Ababa and to travel regularly throughout Africa and internationally. Preferred Master's degree in international relations, public policy, law, business, or a related field. Professional proficiency in French or another African Union working language. Prior experience with the African Union, a diplomatic mission, an international organization, or a major nongovernmental organization. Work Environment And Physical Requirements Professional office environment with regular use of computer monitors and standard office equipment. Ability to sit or stand for extended periods and travel or work outside standard hours when assignments require.

title: Project Director – Integrated Innovation Highway (IIH)
description: PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges. PATH combines scientific and public health expertise, implementation experience, innovation, and strong partnerships with governments, communities, civil society, and development partners. In Ethiopia, PATH works closely with the Federal Ministry of Health, Regional Health Bureaus, health facilities, communities, local organizations, and development partners to strengthen health systems and expand access to high-quality, equitable health services. Project Overview The Integrated Innovation Highway (IIH) is a Gates Foundation-funded project that supports the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) and Ministry of Health (MoH) to develop a government-owned platform that systematically assesses country needs, prioritizes innovations, evaluates evidence and readiness, and supports the transition and scale-up of innovations within the Ethiopian health system. The IIH will establish an integrated approach across six innovation highways: Medical Devices Diagnostics Therapeutics, Family Planning and Nutrition Products Vaccines Technology, including digital health, artificial intelligence (AI), and biotechnology Bundled and Systems Innovations Phase 1 will focus on three tracer products across two highways: Medical Devices: AI-enabled Point-of-Care Ultrasound (AI-POCUS) Diagnostics: Near-Point-of-Care TB PlusLife and Ebola Diagnostics The project will work closely with the Ministry of Health, Regional Health Bureaus, public health institutes, universities, innovators, development partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen innovation governance and develop practical pathways for evaluating, transitioning, and scaling priority health innovations. Position Summary The Project Director will provide overall strategic, technical, and managerial leadership for the Integrated Innovation Highway project. The Project Director will be responsible for the design, planning, implementation, coordination, monitoring, and overall performance of the project. The position will provide strategic and technical guidance to the IIH team and ensure that implementation is aligned with the Government of Ethiopia's priorities, Ministry of Health strategies, and Gates Foundation commitments. The Project Director will serve as a key point of contact for the Ministry of Health, Regional Health Bureaus, Gates Foundation and other donors, grantees, technical partners, and other strategic stakeholders. A central responsibility will be to build and maintain strong relationships with government and ensure that the IIH contributes to a government-owned and sustainable innovation governance and transition-to-scale mechanism, rather than creating parallel systems. The Project Director will report to the PATH Ethiopia Country Director. Key Responsibilities Project Leadership and Management Lead the overall design, planning, implementation, coordination, and review of the IIH project. Develop and oversee annual workplans, implementation plans, budgets, milestones, and deliverables. Provide strategic and technical leadership to the IIH project team. Direct, supervise, mentor, and support project staff and direct reports. Ensure effective coordination across all project workstreams and implementing partners. Monitor project performance and ensure achievement of agreed results and donor commitments. Identify implementation risks, challenges, and bottlenecks and ensure timely corrective actions. Ensure compliance with PATH policies, donor requirements, government requirements, and project agreements. Promote adaptive management, innovation, learning, and continuous improvement. Ministry of Health and Government Engagement Serve as a senior project-level focal point between PATH and the Ministry of Health. Establish and maintain strong relationships with senior MoH officials and relevant directorates, particularly those working on Health Innovation, RMNCH, Quality Improvement and related health-system priorities. Support the Ministry of Health to lead and institutionalize the IIH approach. Facilitate strategic dialogue with MoH on health innovation priorities, evidence, evaluation, financing, transition, and scale. Ensure that IIH activities are aligned with national health strategies, policies, priorities, and systems. Support government-led decision-making and ownership of innovation assessment and transition processes. Facilitate coordination between the MoH, RHBs, public health institutes, universities, professional associations, development partners, innovators, and other relevant stakeholders. title: Junior Lawyer
description: Company Description Abel Zewdu Law Office is a growing legal practice based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, providing counsel and representation to individuals, businesses, and organizations. The office is committed to delivering high-quality legal services with integrity, professionalism, and attention to detail. Team members work closely with clients to understand their needs and offer practical, well-reasoned legal solutions. The firm values continuous learning, ethical practice, and collaboration, creating an environment where junior professionals can develop their skills and advance their careers. Role Description The Junior Lawyer will support the firm’s legal work by assisting with case preparation, legal research, and drafting documents such as contracts, pleadings, opinions, and correspondence. Day-to-day tasks include reviewing laws and regulations, summarizing case files, preparing legal memoranda, and supporting senior lawyers in client meetings, negotiations, and court appearances. The role also involves maintaining organized case records, monitoring deadlines, and coordinating with courts, administrative bodies, and clients as needed. This is a full-time, on-site role based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, requiring regular collaboration with colleagues and direct interaction with clients and stakeholders. Qualifications Law degree (LL.B or equivalent) from an accredited institution and eligibility to practice law in Ethiopia or in the process of obtaining required certification. Strong legal research and analytical skills, including the ability to interpret statutes, case law, and regulations and prepare clear legal memoranda. Proficiency in drafting and reviewing legal documents, contracts, pleadings, and formal correspondence with attention to detail and accuracy. Effective written and verbal communication skills in English and Amharic; additional local or international languages are an advantage. Demonstrated integrity, professionalism, and respect for client confidentiality, with a strong commitment to ethical legal practice. Ability to manage time, handle multiple matters simultaneously, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate in a team, interact with clients, and build professional relationships. Proficiency in standard office software and legal document preparation tools; familiarity with legal research databases is beneficial. Interest in litigation, commercial law, or related practice areas; prior internship or clerkship experience in a law office or court is a plus.

title: Senior Software Sales Engineer

The successful candidate will combine technical knowledge with strong business development and sales skills to understand customer needs, present suitable software solutions, build strategic relationships, and close deals. The role involves managing the complete sales cycle, developing sales strategies, engaging key decision-makers, and collaborating with technical, product, and marketing teams to deliver solutions that meet customer needs and business objectives. Key Responsibilities Develop and execute sales strategies to achieve revenue targets and expand the company's customer base. Identify new markets, generate leads, research competitors, and build a strong pipeline of qualified business opportunities. Build and maintain relationships with key decision-makers, including business owners, executives, IT managers, and corporate clients. Understand customer business challenges and recommend suitable software products, digital platforms, and technology solutions. Conduct product demonstrations, sales presentations, and solution discussions to communicate the value and benefits of proposed solutions. Prepare and present commercial proposals, quotations, and business cases, and negotiate pricing and contract terms within approved limits. Manage the complete sales cycle, from prospecting and lead qualification to negotiation, contract closure, and handover to implementation teams. Maintain accurate sales pipeline records, prepare revenue forecasts, monitor sales performance, and submit regular reports to management. Identify opportunities for upselling, cross-selling, renewals, and long-term customer partnerships. Collaborate with technical, product, and marketing teams to improve sales strategies, respond to customer requirements, and strengthen market positioning. Mentor junior sales staff and support the improvement of sales processes, presentations, and customer engagement practices. Qualifications and Requirements Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field. 3–6 years of relevant experience in software sales, technology sales, B2B sales, or technology business development. Proven track record of achieving sales targets and closing business deals. Experience selling software products, SaaS solutions, enterprise systems, digital platforms, or technology services. Strong understanding of consultative selling, solution-based sales, and software product demonstrations. Proven ability to manage the full sales cycle, prepare proposals, negotiate contracts, and engage senior decision-makers. Familiarity with CRM systems, sales pipeline management, and revenue forecasting. Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship-building skills. The role will contribute to developing the diaspora portfolio, ensuring strategic coherence, implementation quality, and alignment with national priorities, donor requirements and IOM standards. title: Technical Advisor I - Climate
description: Job Description Job title: Technical Advisor I - Climate Job grade: 9 Reporting to: Program Manager I - Early Warning and DRR Department: Country Program Duty location: CRS/Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Term of Employment: Definite term (i.e. up to May 31, 2027) contingent up on availability of funding and performance. Note: This position is for Ethiopian nationals only Job Summary JEOP is an emergency food distribution program targeting transitory food insecure households in more than 120 woredas (districts) designated to JEOP response by EDRMC. The current JEOP consortium led by CRS includes CARE, FH Ethiopia, ORDA Ethiopia, Relief Society of Tigray (REST), and World Vision Ethiopia (WVE). CRS works through local implementing partners Catholic Caritas Ethiopia (CCE)- Harar, CCE-Meki, and CCE - Adigrat. JEOP serves as a food pipeline for up to 33% of the drought-affected woredas in five regions and one city administration (Dire Dawa) across Ethiopia. Your main responsibility includes providing context specific and timely relevant climate information for JEOP operation areas and linking the information with woreda food security analysis tool to enable JEOP conduct quality geographic prioritization and household targeting. Translating climate information into crop and livestock production and productivity is key expectation in this position. In addition, you will also closely work with partners, CRS staff and other stakeholders in developing context specific climate warning and preparedness messages along with key recommendations for communities across JEOP operation areas. You will ensure the messages reach communities in a risk education program under the community based early warning system. As a member of JEOP, you will manage, coordinate, and monitor project activities and relationships with partners and other project stakeholders to assist the achievement of the JEOP early warning system (EWS) objectives, advancing CRS work serving the poor and vulnerable. Your technical skills and knowledge of climate will ensure that the CP delivers high-quality programming and continuously works towards improving the impact of this project. Job Responsibilities Act as the technical lead for JEOP climate analysis and its intersections with other sectors including but not restricted to, early warning, geographic targeting, and household targeting in vulnerability-based targeting (VBT) method. Provide climate-based estimates of crop and livestock production across JEOP woredas and other potential JEOP expansion areas; regularly update the information as seasons change for woredas. Apply climate-based production forecast to the woreda food security analysis tool to better inform geographic and household targeting; regularly update the forecast as seasons change. Provide capacity building training to partners and Government counterparts on mainstreaming climate-based production forecast with woreda food security analysis tool. Identify pocket areas affected by climate related hazards and adjust food security analysis data accordingly. Conduct regular climate analysis, as appropriate to seasonal calendar, and develop and disseminate risk education messages to communities and other stakeholders in JEOP operation areas. Provide monthly context specific climate analysis and forecast for JEOP operation woredas, and potential expansion areas. Taking a quality assurance and improvement lens, support JEOP to strengthen climate sensitive program approaches through a structured review of current programming and guidance in development of quality assurance and improvement tools where needed. Strengthen capacity of JEOP staff (CRS and partners) to represent JEOP in national climate forums including technical working groups and cluster forums. As an active member of CRS’ global climate technical team strengthen JEOP staff access to best and promising practices as well as evolving thinking, as it relates to core EWS objectives. In coordination with JEOP Program Quality colleagues, strengthen integration of climate adaptation and mitigation activities within JEOP programming, ensuring that activities are in line with all humanitarian and SPHERE standards. Support the development and contribute to the implementation of agency-wide, regional and JEOP-specific strategies, standards, tools, and best practices in climate that effectively engage partners, donors and governments. Provide technical solutions remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and how to best apply program design and implementation standards, best practices, partnership principles, tools, and M&E, ensuring high-quality implementation. Contribute to efforts to pre-position CRS for growth opportunities in climate change adaptation and mitigation. Advise design teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities and technic

title: Policy Advisor, Fossil Fuel Transition
description: About Us The International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges. We combine deep expertise across critical policy areas with a collaborative approach to research, advice, and hands-on support that delivers real-world results. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, we are a diverse team of over 300 experts working from offices in Canada and Switzerland as well as other locations around the world. Our research and policy advice help governments, businesses, communities, and civil society make better decisions. Our international Energy Program works with partners across countries and disciplines. We are currently looking for a Policy Advisor, Fossil Fuel Transition, to work within the IISD Energy Program. About The Position The Policy Advisor, Fossil Fuel Transition, will work within IISD’s International Strategy team, helping governments and partners advance a Paris-aligned, just, orderly and equitable transition away from fossil fuel production and consumption, including reform of fossil fuel subsidies and public finance. We recognize the difficult choices facing fossil-fuel-dependent economies: protecting public revenues, energy security, jobs, and affordability while building more resilient and diversified economies. The role involves close collaboration with government counterparts, particularly in the Global South, and with researchers, intergovernmental organizations, and civil society, as well as other teams within IISD’s 50-staff Energy Program and other Institute programs. The Policy Advisor will help design and implement applied research, policy advice, and technical assistance for countries seeking practical transition pathways. For example, the work may examine the effects of changing fossil fuel revenues on government budgets, assess subsidy reform options, or help translate national and international transition commitments into implementable measures. Key responsibilities include Responsibilities Leading policy-oriented research and analysis on fossil fuel transitions, public financial flows, macroeconomic and fiscal risks, subsidies, energy security and economic diversification; translating evidence into actionable options for decision-makers. Designing and managing assigned workstreams and outputs, with clear workplans, responsibilities, quality checks, and milestones; coordinating partners; and contributing to reporting and budget management alongside financial project managers. Building trusted relationships with government counterparts, especially in fossil fuel-dependent economies, as well as knowledge organizations, civil society networks and intergovernmental partners; adapting support to country needs and available evidence. Supporting the development of more junior colleagues through clear task briefs, constructive feedback, peer review, and learning by doing. Contributing to focused funding proposals and partner engagement that build on demonstrated demand and the team’s existing expertise. Working with IISD Communications early in the process to turn research into clear, useful messages and products for intended audiences. About The Successful Applicant We are looking for a thoughtful, self-directed policy professional who combines analytical rigour with practical judgement and reliable delivery. The successful applicant can turn a complex policy question into a workable plan, communicate trade-offs clearly, and work constructively with colleagues across disciplines and time zones. They will understand that fossil fuel-dependent countries face real fiscal, political, and development constraints and will seek credible, country-owned transition solutions rather than one-size-fits-all prescriptions. This is a hands-on role with opportunities to take growing ownership and help develop colleagues. Knowledge And Qualifications The successful applicant will have (essential): A bachelor’s degree or equivalent in economics, public finance, development studies, public policy, natural resource management or a related field. A relevant master’s or PhD degree is an advantage. At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in macroeconomic or fiscal policy, applied economic research, public finance, energy policy, or fossil fuel transitions. Strong strategic thinking, with examples of turning broad questions into concrete outputs and delivering projects to a high standard. A sound understanding of the economic and fiscal implications of energy transition, particularly for countries dependent on fossil fuel production, revenues, or consumption subsidies. Experience engaging government or public-policy stakeholders, preferably in emerging or developing economies, with sensitivity to local institutions, data and policy priorities. Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce concise, persuasive policy notes or propos

title: CHAMP Advisor
description: The role will be based in the WRI Africa Regional Office in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia with regular in-person presence at the Ministry of Planning and Development as required. This is a hybrid position. You will need to be in office at least 8 days per month and living within reasonable commuting distance of the office. About The Program Since launching in 2023, the Coalition for High Ambition Multilevel Partnerships (CHAMP) for Climate Action has quickly developed into a key platform for multilevel climate partnerships. With 77 endorsing countries plus the EU, CHAMP aims to unlock the potential of multilevel partnerships to accelerate NDC implementation, improve access to climate finance for subnational governments, and showcase pioneering action on climate mitigation and adaptation. World Resources Institute (WRI) serves as the CHAMP Secretariat and an important partner supporting CHAMP's governance, diplomatic engagement, communications, national action and research. Job Highlight In this role, you will support Ethiopia's COP32 preparations by ensuring subnational priorities are reflected in the COP32 Action Agenda. You will strengthen collaboration with African CHAMP-endorsing countries, lead regional convenings, and develop evidence-based narratives highlighting the role of subnational governments in climate action. You will be supported by WRI Africa (Ethiopia), the global CHAMP Secretariat team at WRI, and the Ministry of Planning and Development (MoPD). You will report to the Cities Director for Africa, with technical direction and delivery oversight from the Ministry of Planning and Development (MoPD), and work closely with the global CHAMP Secretariat team at WRI. What You Will Do Coordination & Network Facilitation (50%) Support the Ministry of Planning and Development to establish as needed and manage coordination mechanisms linking national ministries, COP32 Secretariat, local government, development partners, NGOs, and civil society, to inform and support subnational and multilevel governance priorities within the COP32 action agenda. Act as a liaison between the MoPD and the COP32 Presidency team and Secretariat on subnational and multilevel governance, providing inputs to Action Agenda planning, thematic days and side events, and tracking follow-up actions. Support communication and coordination efforts around the upcoming IPCC Special Report on Climate Change and Cities, pre- and post-publication, ensuring its findings are integrated into the COP32 process. Contribute to CHAMP's engagement in the 2nd Global Stocktake (GST-2) process to strengthen COP32 outcomes on subnational and multilevel governance, reinforcing the value of local and subnational actors as indispensable partners to national governments for implementation. Regional Convening & Country Engagement (25%) Deepen engagement with African CHAMP-endorsing countries, gathering and synthesizing stories of progress and barriers to effective multilevel partnerships to help shape the COP32 action agenda and showcase the impact of multilevel partnerships at, and in the build-up to, COP32. Lead planning and delivery of Africa regional convenings hosted in partnership with key Ethiopian Ministries, from concept and design through to outputs and follow-up, building regional consensus and momentum in the lead up to COP32. Evidence & Analysis (25%) Inform tracking against relevant Plans to Accelerate Solutions within the Action Agenda, and package findings ahead of COP32 to strengthen the case for Multilevel Partnerships. What You Will Need Education: You have a completed master's degree in environmental policy, sustainable development, urban planning or a related field. Additional experience can be considered in lieu of a degree. Experience: You have 7+ years of full-time relevant work experience in climate policy, subnational governance planning, intergovernmental coordination or a related field, including manager-level experience. Experience in urban policy formulation and strategy development at national and subnational levels. Experience developing frameworks to estimate the contribution of urban to the national economy. Experience engaging with international climate processes (UNFCCC, COP, GST) and translating global frameworks into national/subnational action. Experience organising high-level regional or international convenings. Deep knowledge of Ethiopia's political economy and government structures at national and subnational level. Strong working knowledge of Ethiopia's key planning and investment frameworks, including the 10-Year Development Plan (10 YDP), Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), and Long-Term Low Greenhouse Gas Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS). Established network within Ethiopia, and across the African region and internationally, relevant to climate and subnational governance actors. Experience convening and coordinating across diverse stakeholder groups — government ministries, local government, development

title: Senior Technical Officer - Molecular Virologist (Africa CDC)
description: Job Description AU Values Respect for Diversity and Team Work Think Africa Above all Transparency and Accountability Integrity and Impartiality Efficiency and Professionalism Information and Knowledge Sharing Organization Information Reports to: Head of the Africa CDC Reference Laboratory Directorate/Department: Centre for Laboratory Diagnostics and Systems (CLDS) Division: Centre for Laboratory Diagnostics and Systems (CLDS) Number of Direct Reports: Number of Indirect Reports: Number of Positions: 5 Job Grade: P3 Contract Type: Appointment for Limited duration (ALD) Location: Central Africa Republic (1 position), Ethiopia (4 positions) Purpose of Job The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) is committed to strengthening laboratory systems across the continent to support disease surveillance, outbreak response, and public health emergency preparedness. As part of this commitment, Africa CDC has established the Africa CDC Reference Laboratory, a continental Centre of Excellence for Diagnostics, Research, and Innovation (CEDRI). The Africa CDC Reference Laboratory plays a critical role in supporting laboratory networks across Member States by providing technical assistance to National Public Health Laboratories (NPHLs), particularly where diagnostic capacity is limited and advanced testing is required for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases. This support enhances the continent’s ability to detect, respond to, and prepare for public health threats, including high-consequence pathogens such as Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV). In response to the continued risk of BDBV outbreaks and other public health emergencies in the region, Africa CDC, with support from the World Bank, is recruiting three highly qualified Molecular Virologists (P3) from affected and high-risk Member States. The positions will be based in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Republic of Uganda, and the Republic of South Sudan. Serving as key liaisons between their respective National Public Health Laboratories (NPHLs) and the Africa CDC Reference Laboratory, these locally recruited professionals will strengthen laboratory systems, improve sample referral and management processes, support proficiency testing programs, and enhance outbreak detection and response capacities. Their deployment will further strengthen collaboration between national and continental laboratory networks, contributing to timely disease detection, effective outbreak response, and improved preparedness for public health emergencies across Africa. Main Functions The primary purpose of this role is to support routine and surge molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, and sequencing activities for the response to BDBV outbreaks and other priority pathogens. The Molecular Virologists will serve as key links between the NPHLs and the Africa CDC Reference Laboratory, ensuring effective coordination, timely sample referral and testing, and the exchange of critical laboratory information. Through the provision of advanced technical expertise, they will strengthen national laboratory capacity, enhance diagnostic and sequencing capabilities, and support timely detection, characterization, and response to public health threats. This position aims to strengthen national and continental laboratory capacity and capabilities for the timely detection, characterization and response to outbreaks, through advanced molecular diagnostics, genomic sequencing, laboratory quality management, and oversight of biosafety and biosecurity, as well as technical mentorship Specific Responsibilities Outbreak response and emergency support Serve as the primary technical focal point between the NPHLs in the assigned Member State and the Africa CDC Reference Laboratory during the current EDVB outbreak response and other public health emergencies. Support routine and surge molecular testing activities during outbreaks and public health emergencies, ensuring timely and accurate diagnostic services. Participate in emergency response operations, including extended working hours, field deployments, and other surge-response activities as required. Coordinate the safe, timely, and efficient referral, transport, and tracking of specimens from peripheral testing sites to the NPHL and, when necessary, to the Africa CDC Reference Laboratory. Support forecasting, inventory management, and monitoring of laboratory reagents and consumables, and contribute to procurement planning and supply chain coordination in collaboration with the Africa CDC Reference Laboratory. Facilitate timely communication and reporting of laboratory results, testing volumes, and operational challenges to support evidence-based outbreak response decision-making. Provide technical support to strengthen laboratory preparedness, continuity of operations, and rapid response capacity for high-consequence pathogens, including BDBV. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith. Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories! Employee Contract Type Local - Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term) Job Description Job Purpose : The Clinical Nurse will responsible to under-take planning, implementing, monitoring, and reporting primary health care and nutrition interventions at woreda, health facility, community, and IDP site levels. The position holder will strengthen the quality of health and nutrition services through direct service provision, capacity building, technical support, supervision, and coordination with government health structures and community stakeholders. Major Responsibilities Planning and Coordination Prepare weekly and monthly activity plans in line with approved project work plans and budgets. Develop training plans, schedules, and Terms of Reference (ToRs) for capacity-building activities. Coordinate closely with Woreda Health Offices, health facilities, community structures, and other stakeholders to ensure effective implementation of emergency health interventions. Participate in project review meetings, coordination forums, and emergency response planning activities. Clinical Service Delivery Provide quality primary health care services through health facilities, outreach services, and mobile health teams. Conduct patient assessment, triage, treatment, stabilization, referral, and follow-up according to national treatment guidelines. Deliver maternal, newborn, child health, and reproductive health services, including antenatal and postnatal care. Identify and refer patients requiring specialized or advanced medical care. Ensure adherence to infection prevention and control (IPC) standards and quality-of-care protocols. Health and Nutrition Support Screen and identify malnourished children and pregnant and lactating women for appropriate referral and treatment. Support nutrition-related activities, including community awareness and linkage to nutrition services. Provide health and nutrition education to patients, caregivers, and community members. Emergency Response and Public Health Activities Participate in rapid assessments, baseline assessments, joint assessments, and health facility assessments. Support disease surveillance, early warning, outbreak investigation, and emergency response activities. Assist in the implementation of emergency preparedness and response interventions in affected communities. Monitoring, Reporting, and Documentation Maintain accurate patient records, registers, and service delivery reports. Compile and submit weekly, monthly, and ad hoc reports in a timely manner. Participate in data collection, analysis, monitoring, and evaluation activities. Ensure proper documentation of assessments, referrals, treatments, and project achievements. Required Education, Training, License, Registration, And Certification Bachelor Degree in Nursing with minimum of three years relevant experience. certificate on Clinical case management , PHEM, MHPSS,IMNCI/ICCM/Family planning Required Professional Experience Previous work experience at least 3 years in risk identification, outbreak detection, PHEM, OPD consultation, ICCM/IMNCI, maternal health, and supply chain management areas. Preferred Knowledge And Qualifications Experience in the mobile health and nutrition intervention areas of screening, risk communication, OPD/Inpatient consultation, outreach EPI, health education, sanitation, and child health Language Requirements English & Knowledge of local language is advantageous World Vision is a child-focused organization that is committed to safeguarding all children as well as adult beneficiaries and has zero tolerance for incidents of violence or abuse against children or adults, including sexual exploitation or abuse, committed either by employees or others affiliated with our work. Therefore, World Vision does not hire staff whose background is not suitable for working with children or vulnerable adults, even if their role does not interact directly with them. title: Head of Programs Ethiopia
description:
ForAfrika is an African-rooted, globally connected organisation dedicated to empowering communities across the continent through sustainable development and humanitarian aid. With over 40 years of operational experience, ForAfrika works in environments that vary from emergency relief settings to long-term development, ensuring that every initiative is contextually aligned with the needs of the people it serves. Through a deep love for Africa and unwavering commitment, ForAfrika delivers programmes that transform lives by embracing an integrated approach to development. This includes enhancing education, health and nutrition, water and sanitation, food security and livelihoods, economic empowerment, and more, building environments where all Africans can thrive. Position Summary. The Head of Programs is responsible for leading all programmatic functions across the organization's Mozambique operations, ensuring high-quality, accountable, and sustainable programming that aligns with strategic objectives and responds to community needs. This senior leadership role encompasses oversight of program implementation, quality assurance, community integration, Design, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (DMEAL), and emergency response coordination. The successful candidate will provide visionary leadership to drive program excellence while building organizational capacity and fostering partnerships that amplify impact. Reporting Relationships The Head of Programs has a solid-line reporting relationship to the Country Director and a dotted-line relationship to the Director of Programs, Global Support Office who provides technical oversight, guidance, and capacity building on programmatic matters. This relationship includes: Regular program quality reviews and discussions Technical support and guidance on program design and implementation Collaborative development of country-specific program strategies Knowledge exchange on innovative approaches and best practices Capacity building initiatives for the country program team Key Roles and Responsibilities Strategic Program Leadership & Quality Assurance Provide strategic direction and oversight for all programmatic activities across multiple sectors including health, education, WASH, food security, livelihoods, and emergency response Establish and maintain program quality frameworks ensuring adherence to international standards including SPHERE, Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), and donor compliance requirements Lead the development and implementation of the country program strategy in alignment with organizational mission and donor requirements Ensure all programs are designed and implemented in ways responsive to community needs, cultural contexts, and beneficiary feedback Champion innovation in program design and implementation methodologies to enhance effectiveness and sustainability 2. Program Implementation Management Oversee portfolio of programs with collective budgets and ensure efficient resource allocation across initiatives Monitor program performance against targets, timelines, and budgetary allocations, implementing corrective measures as needed Lead program proposal development processes, ensuring technical quality, contextual relevance, and competitive positioning Coordinate with finance team on budget variance analysis (BVA) and financial reporting to ensure fiscal accountability Establish and maintain relationships with key donors, government partners, and implementing partners 3.Community Integration & Partnership Development Ensure meaningful community participation in all phases of program cycle from design through evaluation Establish and maintain strategic partnerships with local organizations, government entities, and community leaders Lead development of community engagement strategies that promote local ownership and sustainability Oversee capacity building initiatives for community-based organizations and local partners Ensure cultural sensitivity and conflict-sensitive programming approaches across all interventions 4. Emergency Response & Humanitarian Coordination Lead organizational preparedness for emergency response including development and regular updating of contingency plans Coordinate rapid response to humanitarian crises, ensuring timely and effective assistance delivery Represent the organization in humanitarian coordination forums and cluster meetings Maintain emergency supply stocks and ensure readiness of response teams and equipment Lead needs assessments and response strategy development during humanitarian emergencies 5. Team Leadership & Organizational Development Provide leadership and mentorship to program managers, MEAL officers, field coordinators, and technical specialists Build organizational capacity through staff development planning, training coordination, and performance management Foster collaborative work environment that promotes professional growth and high performance Establish clear performance expectations and accountability mechanisms for all program staff Champion organizational values and ensure adherence to code of conduct and safeguarding policies 6. External Relations & Representation Serve as primary liaison with donors, government officials, and partner organizations on programmatic matters Represent the organization at national and international forums, conferences, and coordination meetings Develop and maintain strategic relationships that enhance program effectiveness and organizational profile Lead resource mobilization efforts and contribute to fundraising strategy development Ensure compliance with government regulations and maintain positive relationships with authorities Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Degree in development related studies- Agriculture, Range management, Natural Resource Management, Economics, Social sciences or related field Professional certifications in project/program management (PMP, PMD Pro) preferred Minimum 8-10 years of progressive experience in international development or humanitarian programming At least 5 years in senior management roles Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-sector programs in Sub-Saharan Africa, preferably Mozambique Experience in emergency response coordination and humanitarian programming Technical Competencies Expert knowledge of program cycle management and quality frameworks Strong understanding of international humanitarian and development standards (SPHERE, CHS, HAP) Proficiency in DMEAL methodologies, evaluation techniques, and data analysis Knowledge of major donor requirements (USAID, EU, UN agencies, bilateral donors) Understanding of conflict-sensitive programming and Do No Harm approaches Leadership & Management Skills Exceptional leadership capabilities with experience managing diverse, multicultural teams Strong strategic thinking and analytical skills with ability to translate vision into operational plans Excellent communication and presentation skills in English; local language skills advantageous Proven ability to build and maintain relationships with diverse stakeholders Experience in organizational development and capacity building Personal Attributes Strong commitment to humanitarian principles and development values Cultural sensitivity and ability to work effectively in diverse environments High degree of flexibility and adaptability to changing circumstances Results-oriented with strong attention to detail and quality Integrity and commitment to ethical programming practices Working Conditions Position based in Ethiopia with regular travel to field locations (up to 40% travel) Willingness to work in challenging environments and respond to emergency situations Flexibility to work extended hours during crisis response or critical program periods Commitment to maintaining security protocols and organizational safety standards

title: Development of a vector control training package for wash and health practitioners in the africa region.
description:
(Find the complete folder with all relevant information including the RFP here ) Terms of Reference Title of Assignment Development of a Vector Control Training Package for WASH and Health Practitioners in the Africa Region Project Name WASH Surge Localization Programme Project Country Global (pilot training to be conducted in Ethiopia or South Sudan) 1. Introduction The Netherlands Red Cross (NLRC) and partners are working to strengthen local capacities for emergency preparedness, anticipatory action, and response across Africa. In line with their auxiliary role to the public authorities, and within the framework of localization, National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies frequently act as first responders during disease outbreaks, flooding, displacement crises, and other emergencies. Vector-borne diseases continue to pose a significant public health burden in many countries where the Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies operate. At the same time, vector control knowledge among WASH and Health practitioners varies considerably. There is a need for accessible, practical training materials that can be used by National Societies, surge personnel, and humanitarian practitioners to improve knowledge and decision-making related to vector control. The NLRC therefore seeks a consultant to develop a comprehensive training package on vector control that can be delivered by facilitators with a fair understanding of the subject matter. The package will be piloted during a training event planned for December 2026 in either Ethiopia or South Sudan. 2. Background and Context Vector-borne diseases remain among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in many humanitarian settings. Climate change, population movements, urbanization, environmental degradation, and weak health systems are contributing to changes in disease transmission patterns and increasing the risk of outbreaks. Humanitarian organizations are increasingly expected to integrate vector control considerations into emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programmes. While specialist expertise is sometimes available, many WASH and Health practitioners involved in programme design and implementation have limited formal training in vector control. The Red Cross movement has an important role to play through: Community engagement , risk communication and behaviour change Environmental management Vector surveillance and risk assessment Support to outbreak preparedness and response including community-based surveillance Coordination with health and WASH actors Integration of vector control into humanitarian programming To strengthen these capacities, a practical training package is required that can be delivered in different country contexts and adapted to local disease priorities. 3. Purpose, Objectives and Deliverables Purpose To develop a practical, participatory and easy-to-facilitate vector control training package for WASH and Health practitioners working in humanitarian and development settings. Overall Objective To increase the knowledge and understanding of vector-borne disease prevention and vector control among WASH and Health practitioners, enabling them to support the design, implementation and monitoring of appropriate vector control interventions. Specific Objectives The training package should enable participants to: Understand the epidemiology and transmission pathways of major vector-borne diseases. Understand the roles and responsibilities of WASH, Health and community actors in vector control. Conduct basic vector-related risk assessments. Select appropriate vector control interventions based on context and risk. Understand operational, environmental and safety considerations. Integrate vector control into preparedness, anticipatory action and humanitarian emergency responses. Coordinate with relevant health, WASH and government stakeholders. Scope of the Training Package The consultant should develop a 3 days training package with different modules and exercises, allowing for a one to three days training depending on the modules used. The training should cover, at minimum: Vector-borne Diseases Introduction to: Malaria (with description of different malaria carrying subspecies) Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever, Schistosomiasis, Trypanosomiasis and other relevant diseases common in African humanitarian settings Vector Control Approaches Introduction to Environmental mechanical biological and chemical and integrated Vector Management (IVM). Humanitarian Context The context considered for the training include, vector control during emergencies**,** vector control during displacement and camp settings, Flood-related vector risks, Urban vector control challenges as well as for the Red Cross important Community-based approaches, and Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI) Planning and Decision Making The training should include a section focusing on health and surveillance data, risk assessment, Intervention selection, Monitoring and evaluation, Coordination mechanisms Safety and Environmental Considerations This should include Safe handling of equipment and chemicals Environmental risks Waste management Safeguarding and community acceptance Emerging and other relevant Topics Climate change and vector-borne diseases Insecticide resistance, new and emerging vector control tools such as spatial repellents, Operational challenges in humanitarian settings Deliverables The consultant will with the support of the NLRC and UNICEF will be expected to provide: Review and compilation of existing vector control training materials from organizations such as: IFRC, WHO, UNICEF and NGO’s working on vector control and identify materials that can be adapted and referenced. The consultant will develop a complete facilitator package in English including: Facilitator guide, Agenda for a 3-day version, Session plans, Facilitation notes, Interactive exercises Possible case studies and group work exercises, Quizzes and knowledge checks Participant package that should include: Participant manual, Handouts, Reference materials, Reading list Links to online resources PowerPoint presentation deck(s) suitable for use by non-specialist facilitators. Training evaluation package including: Pre-training assessment Post-training assessment Participant evaluation forms Facilitation of a pilot training in December 2026 in Ethiopia South Sudan or other country in the region and incorporation of lessons learned into the final training package(optional). 4. Profile of the Desired Consultant The consultant should possess: Minimum 7 years of professional experience in vector control, public health, entomology, or related fields. Demonstrated experience in humanitarian settings. Experience with vector control in Africa, preferably in both emergency and development contexts. Proven experience in developing training curricula and adult learning materials. Strong facilitation skills. Experience working with Red Cross/Red Crescent, UN agencies, government institutions or international NGOs is an advantage. Excellent written and spoken English. Experience integrating participatory adult learning methodologies. 5. Methodology The consultant is expected to: Conduct a brief desk review of existing training resources. Consult with NLRC, IFRC, UNICEF and selected technical experts. Develop draft training materials. Revise materials based on feedback. Facilitate the pilot training.
